transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I'm here because my talking gets all mixed up. I'll try to explain something to people, you know, about the keys, and then... then the jail, or the prayer rug, and then chess pieces. And people just tell me they cannot follow what I am saying. It just gets all jumbled up when I try to talk.
Are you often confused about where you are or what day it is?
No, not really. I know I'm at the clinic, and I know it's Tuesday. I don't get lost like that. It's just the talking that gets tangled.
Have you had times when your mood was unusually high or expansive?

Yeah, I do get like that. There are times I just feel... I don't know, so high and powerful. I'll be laughing and talking real loud with everyone I see. But then, if someone questions me about something, even just a small thing, I can snap. I'll just start shouting right at them.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people do not?

Yeah, I do. Sometimes I hear a man's voice. It comes from the vents, or... or sometimes out of the mop closet at work. He says my name, or he tells me that I ruined everything. And it's not just a thought, you know? It sounds exactly as real as someone standing right beside me.
Have you ever had the voices or the confused speech when your mood was not unusually high or irritable?

Yeah, I have. There have been... well, calmer weeks, I guess. Times when my mood wasn't really high or angry, and I wasn't deeply depressed either. Just regular. But even during those times, for more than two weeks straight, I still heard that man in the vents. And I still believed the people working in the building were making signals about me to each other. So, yeah, it happens even when my mood is fine.
Have you ever used alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or any other drugs before these symptoms started?
No, I haven't. I mean, I might have a beer every now and then, but I don't use drugs. Never touched cannabis or stimulants or anything like that. These things just... they happen on their own.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was so elevated or irritable that you needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I have. There are times when I just... I feel so high and, I don't know, powerful. Like I'm on top of the world. I don't need much sleep at all during those times. I'll just be laughing and talking loud with everyone, feeling great. But... well, if someone questions me or gets in my way, I can snap. I get really irritable and I might just shout at them over some small thing. It changes fast like that.
During those times when you feel very high or irritable and need much less sleep, have you ever had to be hospitalized or been unable to keep up with work or daily responsibilities because of it?

Yeah, I have. It... it gets pretty bad. I've missed shifts and ended up losing cleaning work because of it. I've also stopped going to the mosque and joining in on family gatherings. My family and the people there, they say they can't rely on me, or that they just can't understand me when I'm acting like that. And... well, yeah, there have been times when I was unsafe enough that other people actually had to call for emergency help. So, yes, it definitely stops me from keeping up with my life.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very down or lost interest or pleasure in almost everything?

Yeah, I have those times too. It usually lasts a while, definitely more than two weeks. On my bad days, I just... I sit on the edge of the bed after morning prayer and I feel so heavy. Just empty. Like there's no point in even cleaning myself up or going outside. I just don't care about anything when it gets like that.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were not having any major mood symptoms, but you were still hearing voices or having other psychotic symptoms?

Yeah, I have. There have been calmer weeks where I wasn't feeling especially high, and I wasn't deeply depressed either. Just... normal, I guess. But even then, for more than two weeks straight, I still heard the man in the vents. And I still believed the people in the building I clean were signaling to each other about me. So, yes, those things were still happening even when my mood was fine.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt so unusually energized or high that you were clearly different from your usual self?

Yes, I have. Sometimes I get this feeling where I'm just... so up. Like I'm really powerful or important, and I have all this energy. I'll be talking really loud, laughing with everyone I see, just feeling on top of the world. But... it can flip pretty fast. If someone questions what I'm doing or gets in my way, even over something small, I can just snap. I'll start shouting at them. It's like I'm on a hair-trigger when I get like that. And yeah, it definitely lasts for a week or more when it happens.
Have there ever been times when you were hearing voices or having paranoid beliefs for at least two weeks while your mood was completely normal?

Yeah, I think I mentioned this a minute ago, but yes. Like I said, there have been calmer weeks where my mood was completely fine. I wasn't especially high, and I wasn't deeply depressed either. But even during those normal weeks... for more than two weeks, I still heard the man in the vents. And I still believed the people in the building I clean were making signals about me. So yeah, those things still happen even when my mood is normal.
Have you ever had at least two weeks of hallucinations or delusions when you were not having a manic or depressive episode?

Yeah, I think we just went over this, but yes. I've had times, definitely more than two weeks, where my mood was just fine. I wasn't manic, wasn't depressed, just... normal. But the whole time, I was still hearing that guy talking in the vents. And I still knew the people at work were making those signals about me. So, the mood stuff stops, but the other stuff doesn't.
Have you also had a period of at least one week when your mood was unusually high or irritable, without a major depressive episode at the same time?

Yeah, I think that's what I was saying earlier. There are definitely weeks where I'm not down or depressed at all, just... really, really up. Like I said, I get this feeling of being so powerful and high, laughing and talking loud with everybody. But it's like a switch, you know? If someone gets in my way or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. I'll shout at them over the smallest thing. So yeah, I get that high and irritable feeling without being depressed.
Have there ever been times when your mood was completely normal and you were still hearing voices or having paranoid beliefs?

Yeah, doc, I'm pretty sure we keep covering this same exact thing. But yes. 

Like I've been saying, there are calmer weeks. Times when I'm not especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed either. Just regular. But even during those times, for more than two weeks, I still hear the man in the vents. And I still believe the people in the building are making signals about me. My mood being normal doesn't make that go away.
